newsitem.title: PERU: LIMA SHARE PRICES END SLIGHTLY UP IN THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: LIMA SHARE PRICES END SLIGHTLY UP IN THIN TRADE.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed slightly up Monday in thin trade as foreign investors looked to make gains on other markets in the region, brokers said.
They added a similar trend was likely Tuesday.
Monday, the General Index edged up 0.40 percent to 2,060.6 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index nudged 0.17 percent higher to 2,963.0 points.
In a total of 1,216 trades, volume was 27.0 million soles ($10.2 million), according to brokers.

"We continue to see little money coming in. There is no serious trading in the main stocks and you only see speculative buying," Manuel Torres of local brokerage Finvest said. "We hope now that markets abroad have begun to fall, some money will fall our way."

Peru's leading financial services holding company Credicorp gained 1.96 percent to close at $20.80 on volume of 34,600 shares. ING Barings said Monday it had reiterated its buy recommendation for the company.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru climbed 0.47 percent to 6.39 soles on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Peru's largest brewery group UCP Backus rose 0.86 percent to 2.35 soles on volume of 749,000 shares.
